newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students holed up on university campus.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students holed up on university campus.

text.p: More than 700 South Korean students were holed up at Seoul's Hanyang University on Tuesday after fierce fighting on Monday evening left one police officer dead, prosecution officials said.
They said more than 2,000 students slipped away from the scene of the worst violence in almost a year and headed to Seoul National University to spend the night.

Media reports on Tuesday said one student underwent brain surgery after suffering a serious blow to the head on Monday when students battled riot police with petrol bombs and wielded heavy metal pipes.
Hospital officials confirmed the student was Yoo Soo from Joong-ang University but provided no details of his condition. Media reports said the student's life was not in danger.
The chief prosecutor on Monday ordered a round-up of organisers from the outlawed leftist Hanchongryon and demanded that they be "severely punished".
Kim Ki-soo also ordered the arrest of "criminals" responsible for the death of the 21-year-old officer, signalling that another harsh crackdown on students may be imminent.

But militant students planned to push forward on Tuesday with an inaugural ceremony to kick off the Hanchongryon's new leadership. It was originally scheduled for Friday but has been delayed as police have blocked off Hanyang University, which was chosen as the venue.

The capital braced for a fifth day as students were expected to converge on the university campus at 2 p.m. (0300 GMT). Squadrons of police backed by armoured teargas launchers surrounded the campus to prevent the rally.
The four days of violence has been the worst campus agitation since the government crushed a student rebellion at Yonsei University last August.

On Monday, witnesses said a number of police officers were beaten senseless as thousands of students brandishing heavy metal pipes and hurling firebombs burst through a security cordon outside Hanyang University.
Students have been staging hit-and-run raids on police squads posted in downtown areas by cruising the subway system and emerging without warning to hurl rocks and firebombs.

Violence that has left large areas of Seoul strewn with rubble, smashed glass and spent teargas canisters was sparked by President Kim's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election.
Allegations that Kim grossly overspent have surfaced in the final year of his presidency in the wake of a corruption scandal involving loans to the Hanbo Group.
The Hanbo scandal has led to the arrest of Kim's second son and shattered his credibility.
